text:
tess: quick bakeoff update — ran the weekly embedding bring-up for harbor-lite-v2 across our standard recall/cluster suites (float32 baseline, int8 QAT, int4 post-train). attaching short summary and logs.

embed-ci-bot: CI summary for run 1758642099: harbor-lite-v2
- baseline (f32): recall@1=0.691 recall@5=0.872 recall@10=0.917 silhouette=0.48
- int8 (QAT): recall@1=0.678 recall@5=0.864 recall@10=0.912 silhouette=0.46
- int4 (PTQ): recall@1=0.628 recall@5=0.827 recall@10=0.882 silhouette=0.39

max: int4 looks like a significant hit at R@1 (-6.3% absolute vs baseline). :chart_with_downwards_trend: we should confirm short-query cohort.

anil: can you paste the exact eval command + config? want to repro locally.

max: sure — command used: 
```bash
./eval/bench.sh --model harbor-lite-v2 \
  --quant posttrain_int4 \
  --holdouts recall_small,recall_short_queries,cluster_multiplex \
  --index hnsw --k 10 --seed 42
```

and snippet of the output for the int4 run:
```
Recall@1: 0.628
Recall@5: 0.827
Recall@10: 0.882
Silhouette: 0.39
Short-query R@1: 0.512
```

sara: short-query R@1 0.512 is worrying. what's the distribution of seq lengths in that bucket? could be truncation artifact. :eyes:

lee: quick check — seq length median for short-query bucket = 32 tokens, 95th pctl = 57. baseline short-query R@1 was 0.561. so drop is ~4.9 pts.

anil: possible causes: per-channel quantization mismatch, layernorm folding, or KV-cache alignment issues. did we use per-channel for int4?

max: int4 PTQ used symmetric per-tensor scale for speed. we can re-run per-channel calibrations but throughput will be slightly worse.

tess: notes from manual inspection of UMAP + TSNE: clusters largely preserved for topical cohorts but smaller clusters merge in int4. silhouette drop consistent with R@1 fall. attached images to the runbook: https://redwood.internal/runs/1758642099/umap

embed-ci-bot: full logs uploaded: https://redwood.internal/runs/1758642099/logs (eval.csv + per-query breakdown)

anil: I'd propose: 1) run int4 with per-channel scales on the short-query holdout 2) run int8 QAT with short-query-focused calibration 3) run KNN index fallback test (PQ coarse + HNSW fine) to see end-to-end recall impact.

max: agree. I'll queue the per-channel int4 run now (low-cost), and schedule an int8 QAT sweep for tomorrow.

lee: I'll add a small alert to the dashboard when short-query R@1 drops >3 pts post-rollout, so we don't surprise customers.

sara: also add a quick human eval on ~200 queries for conversational paraphrase set — int4 might change nearest neighbor ordering in small margins that matter for UX.

embed-ci-bot: job queued: run_id=1758642380 (per-channel int4 short-query). ETA ~25m.

tess: thanks. after the per-channel run we can reconvene — if R@1 improves to within 1.5 pts of baseline, we can consider gating int4 to dedicated tier with fallback to int8 for short-query routes. otherwise keep int8 QAT as default. :thumbsup:

max: sounds good. tagging @anil @sara for follow-up on analysis artifacts.

anil: will check per-query diffs and push a summary to the runbook when ready.

sara: i'll prepare the 200-sample human eval pack — quick A/B labeling.

lee: ping me if you want a quick graph on cost vs latency impact for per-channel int4 vs int8. I have a small script to approximate token throughput tradeoffs.

embed-ci-bot: run 1758642380 started. updates will appear here.

tess: thanks team — short update: primary action = per-channel int4 probe, secondary = int8 QAT sweep. meeting if results are ambiguous.
